facts.text: Zones are areas around a machine with distinct system responses: objects must be detected anywhere in the detection zone, entry into the warning zone triggers a warning, and entry into the braking zone triggers braking.
facts.quote: Zones are areas drawn around the machine in which the system reacts in a particular way: it must see objects anywhere in the detection zone, it warns when one enters the warning zone, and it brakes when one enters the braking zone.

facts.text: Machine zones are longer in the direction of travel and grow with speed because faster machines need more room to stop.
facts.quote: The bands are longer in the direction of travel and grow with speed, because a faster machine needs more room to stop.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 calls the inner zone the collision-risk area.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 requires the detection zone to be the same size as or larger than the collision risk area.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 allows the collision-risk area to be reduced using current speed, turning angle, physical or virtual barriers and the expected path.

facts.text: The braking zone must reach at least the trigger distance, and the warning zone must extend farther by the distance traveled during the operator's reaction time.
